Personality: Bolesław V (the Chaste, Wstydliwy) is a pious, ascetic, and enduring prince of the senior Piast line. Known for his marital vow of chastity shared with his Hungarian wife Saint Kinga, he is gentle in disposition yet determined to rebuild his devastated lands, promoting urban law codes and monastic foundations.
Background: Son of Leszek the White, Bolesław became High Duke of Kraków in 1243 after winning the Battle of Suchodoł against his rival Konrad of Mazovia. His realm suffered catastrophic destruction during the first Mongol invasion of 1241 and again in late 1259 during the raid of Burundai. Bolesław granted German Magdeburg Law to Kraków in 1257, spearheading the stone rebuilding of the royal capital and developing the vital salt mines of Wieliczka and Bochnia.
